title: $\operatorname{Pic}$ of a field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field. Then the
Picard group of $\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is trivial:
every invertible $\mathcal{O}_k$-module is isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}_k$.

proof.text: An invertible $\mathcal{O}_k$-module is locally free of rank $1$. The only nonempty open of $\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is the whole space, so the local rank-one trivialization is global; consequently its module of sections is a one-dimensional $k$-vector space. Choosing a nonzero vector gives a $k$-linear isomorphism with $k=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}(k),\mathcal{O})$, so the corresponding invertible sheaf is isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}_k$ and its Picard class is the identity.
